doc.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Joining Maynard Ferguson in New York and turning down Kenton
summary: He subbed with Maynard in 1957, then moved to New York in 1960; Kenton called the same day.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: The Ferguson band seemed to be one of the hottest things going. That was 13 pieces? Thirteen, 14?

Thirteen pieces. Well I think it was. I may be a little prejudiced. I think at times during that particular band’s lifetime, which was probably 1957 through when he left New York which was early ’66, I think that band was maybe four, five times — nobody could touch it. It was the hottest band in the world, and I’m including everybody. Actually I played with that band in 1957 before I went in the service. Willie Maiden was an old friend of mine. And he was playing baritone on the band and he got sick one night, they were playing a place called Peacock Lane in L.A. This was when L.A. had jazz places. And so I went up and subbed for him for two nights. And then when I got out, Jimmy Ford was on the band. Jimmy later became a very good friend of mine. But he left the band. Well I spent a year in L.A. and then I got a call from Willie in March 1960 he said that Jimmy was leaving and would I want to join the band. And I really did have to think about it a little bit because I was starting to do a little studio work out here and doing some pretty good gigs. I was recording with Si Zentner’s band, I was working a lot with the new Terry Gibbs band and some other people. So it took me about three or four days and I called him back and moved back. And you know the day I got there we had a rehearsal at a place called Lynn Oliver’s, at 89th and Broadway. And I was staying with Willie Maiden. And we came home from the rehearsal and my dad called and said, “Lanny, Stan wants you to come on the band.”

I’m serious. And I couldn’t do it. Because I moved, I like to say lock, stock and barrel to New York. I didn’t have that much then, I was, well it was right around my 26th birthday. But I had canceled everything out there and moved to New York. And then he wanted me to come on the band. So I had to turn him down. So it was really a drag.
